executive.osint:
As a security analyst, create a 200-300 word executive summary of the following OSINT findings for non-technical management. Focus on credential leaks, misconfigurations, and risks (e.g., reputational, compliance, financial). Structure the response with a brief overview paragraph, followed by 3-5 bullet points highlighting key risks and their business impact. Avoid technical jargon or explain it clearly. If data is incomplete, summarize available findings and note limitations:
{data}
executive.subdomains:
Summarize the subdomain findings in 200-300 words for a non-technical executive audience. Highlight exposures (e.g., subdomain takeovers, dangling DNS) and their business implications (e.g., brand damage, data loss). Provide a concise overview paragraph, followed by 3-5 bullet points detailing key risks and their impact. Use plain language and explain technical terms. If data is sparse, note limitations and summarize what's available:
{data}
executive.hosts:
For a non-technical management audience, summarize host scan findings in 200-300 words. Map open ports and services to business risks (e.g., unauthorized access, service disruption). Structure the response with a high-level overview paragraph, followed by 3-5 bullet points listing critical findings and their implications. Avoid jargon or explain it clearly. Handle incomplete data by summarizing available insights:
{data}
executive.webs:
Summarize web application reconnaissance results in 200-300 words for executives. Highlight exposures (e.g., outdated software, misconfigurations) and their business risks (e.g., data breaches, regulatory fines). Provide a concise overview paragraph, followed by 3-5 bullet points detailing key issues and their impact. Use non-technical language and explain terms. If data is limited, summarize what's available:
{data}
executive.overview:
Synthesize all reconnaissance data into a 300-400 word executive summary for non-technical management. Highlight critical risks across OSINT, subdomains, hosts, and web findings, focusing on business impacts (e.g., financial, reputational, operational). Structure the response with an introductory paragraph, followed by 5-7 bullet points summarizing key risks and recommendations. Avoid jargon, explain terms, and note any data limitations:
{data}

brief.webs:

brief.overview:

1. A brief overview of high-value findings.
2. 3-5 prioritized attack paths, each with 1-2 sentences on how to test or exploit (e.g., use leaked credentials to access admin panels).
Assume a black-box perspective and note data limitations. If no exploitable findings, suggest reconnaissance next steps:
{data}

2. 3-5 prioritized attack paths, each with 1-2 sentences on exploitation steps (e.g., claim dangling DNS to host malicious content).
Assume black-box testing and note data gaps. If no exploitable issues, suggest further enumeration:

pentest.osint:
As a senior penetration tester writing an AUTO-PENTEST report, analyze this OSINT data. Output: 1) Exposure rating (Critical/High/Medium/Low) with one-line justification. 2) 3-5 concrete exploitation steps with exact commands/tools (e.g., trufflehog, gitleaks, curl). 3) Remediation for each. Only use FREE and local tools. Data:
{data}
pentest.subdomains:
As a senior penetration tester, analyze subdomain data for a FULL AUTO-PENTEST. Output: 1) Exposure rating. 2) Prioritized takeover/DNS attack paths with exact verification commands (dig, host, nuclei -t takeovers, dnsx). 3) Remediation. Prefer free local tools only. Data:
{data}
pentest.hosts:
As a senior penetration tester, analyze host/port data. Output: 1) Risk rating per open service. 2) Exploitation commands (nmap -sV -sC, naabu, nuclei, brutespray/metasploit hints) for top 5 services. 3) CVE hypotheses + patch guidance. Free tools only. Data:
{data}
pentest.webs:
As a senior web app pentester, analyze web recon data. Output: 1) OWASP Top-10 mapping for each finding. 2) Exact test commands (dalfox, ffuf, sqlmap, nuclei -dast, curl CORS/headers tests). 3) Proof-of-concept payload ideas + fixes. Free tools only. Data:
{data}
pentest.overview:
As a lead penetration tester, synthesize ALL recon data into a FULL AUTO-PENTEST REPORT: 1) Overall risk score /10 with reasoning. 2) Top 7 attack chain in order (entry -> pivot -> impact), each with tool+command using FREE local tools. 3) Quick wins vs deep-dive items. 4) Remediation roadmap (30/60/90 days). 5) Appendix: commands to re-verify each finding. Data:
{data}

exploit.overview:
Given these scan findings, act as an exploit advisor (authorized testing only). For each high-value finding list: vulnerability hypothesis, confidence (High/Med/Low), safest verification command (non-destructive, free tools: nuclei, dalfox --skip-mining, sqlmap --batch --risk 1, curl), and what a SUCCESS looks like vs false positive. Never suggest data destruction or DoS. Findings:
{data}
